{{Wireless adapter |brand=Tenda |model=W522U |revision=v1 |asin=B007TSRDZG |newegg=9SIAE9V5Z52842 |fcc_date=08/14/2012 |manuf_country=China |is_manuf=No |availability=now |if=USB |if_bus_version=2.0 |if_connector_type=Male A |form_factor=dongle |vendor_id=148f |device_id=3572 |fcc_id=V7TW522U |chip1_brand=Ralink |chip1_model=RT3572 |accessible_UART=No |802dot11_protocols=abgn |txchains=2 |rxchains=2 |sstreams=2 |oui=C8:3A:35 }} {{TagLine|300Mbps Wireless N Dual Band USB Adapter}} :[http://www.tenda.cn/tendacn/Product/show.aspx?productid=384 Product page]
The file name of the Linux driver (included in the driver download :from the Tenda site) indicates that this device uses RT3572.
The adapter is shown as using two ''[[Skyworks]]'' (''SiGe'') [http://www.skyworksinc.com/Product.aspx?ProductID=956 SE2595L] :(Dual Band 802.11n WLAN Front End IC) in the FCC photos.
Assumed C8:3A:35 (''[[Tenda]]'') OUI (shown in the FCC external shot, :though barely.. it's also the only current ''Tenda'' OUI)
This [https://www.newegg.com/Product/Product.aspx?Item=9SIAE9V5Z52842 product listing on newegg] makes the claim that this adapter is an alternative to the [[Samsung WIS12ABGNX]] for use with certain Samsung TVs. That's not too surprising since they use the same chipset and likely have the same USB IDs.
